content: The importance of vaccination cannot be overstated, both for the general public and healthcare workers. A significant challenge in the European Region is the lack of political commitment and advocacy for the elimination of measles and rubella. The WHO Regional Office must collaborate closely with Member States to elevate the priority of measles and rubella elimination at national and subnational levels. This will ensure the allocation of necessary resources to enhance and sustain routine immunization programs. The awareness and perceptions of both healthcare professionals and the public are critical in achieving immunization goals. Vaccine hesitancy has emerged as a growing issue in the Region, driven by factors such as complacency (a lack of concern about measles and rubella), distrust in vaccines and the authorities delivering them, insufficient recommendations from healthcare providers, and limited access to convenient immunization services. Immediate action is required to address these barriers, targeting caregivers, parents, healthcare workers, and underserved or marginalized populations through both traditional and innovative communication channels. High-level advocacy efforts are essential to emphasize the importance of elimination goals and the resources required to maintain and improve immunization programs. These efforts include advocacy visits coordinated with WHO headquarters, involving Regional Office staff, members of the Regional Verification Commission, key partners, and immunization ambassadors. The Regional Office will also mobilize its Regional Director to deliver key messages during routine correspondence and meetings with health ministers. Additionally, high-visibility events, such as side meetings at the Regional Committee and World Health Assembly, will be organized to advocate for measles and rubella elimination. The European Immunization Week (EIW), established in 2005 and held annually in April, has proven to be an effective platform for immunization advocacy. Its objective is to increase vaccination coverage by raising awareness of the importance of immunization, particularly among vulnerable groups. With participation from 53 Member States, EIW has become one of the most visible pan-European health initiatives. The Regional Office will continue to coordinate and strengthen the EIW platform, ensuring its effectiveness in communicating the benefits of immunization and elimination goals. Healthcare workers play a pivotal role in providing parents with accurate information and access to quality prevention services, particularly immunization programs. Despite the abundance of vaccine-related information available today, parents often rely on their children’s healthcare providers for guidance on vaccination. The Regional Office will support healthcare professionals by disseminating high-quality information on vaccines, vaccine-preventable diseases, and the importance of elimination targets. This will be achieved through the publication of periodicals, scientific reports, promotional materials, and updates on the Regional Office’s website. Infographics and job aids will also be developed and made available for use by Member States and partners. Recognizing the growing influence of online media and bloggers, the Regional Office will strengthen its online and social media presence to communicate key advocacy and awareness messages about measles and rubella. A bloggers for health strategy will be implemented to leverage bloggers as reliable sources of information for parents and healthcare workers. The Regional Office will also assist Member States in enhancing their online presence by refining the immunization pages of official ministry websites. To address vaccine safety concerns, the Regional Office launched guidelines in 2013 to help health officials manage communication responses to vaccine safety events, such as adverse events following immunization (AEFI) or rumors. Training on vaccine safety communications will be developed and piloted, with further implementation planned. The Regional Office will also provide ad-hoc safety communication support to Member States as needed. Technical assistance will be provided to Member States experiencing measles or rubella outbreaks, public confidence crises, declining vaccine uptake, or low healthcare worker support for immunization. This assistance will include capacity building in communication and campaign design, leveraging the Regional Office’s expertise in behavior change communications, health promotion, and social mobilization. The elimination of measles and rubella in the European Region requires the support of regional and global partners. This support may include advocating for adequate resources, providing technical assistance and policy guidance, sharing best practices, and offering direct resources. The Regional Office will work to revive the MECACAR platform, which has previously demonstrated success in coordinating immunization efforts across multiple countries. Strengthening partnerships with donors, ministries of health, and other organizations will be essential to achieving elimination goals.
